gen-fs-red-hat-display-inter: Red Hat Display draws every line like a marker, with daylight inside each curve. Inter has the taller lowercase and the smooth, tube-like finish, so it quietly carries the reading while the heading makes the statement.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-poppins: Marker-bold and contemporary, Red Hat Display holds the top with open curves and a constant stroke. And Poppins, sturdy and tall in the lowercase, follows with loose, unknotted curves that never flicker thick to thin.
gen-fs-rosaline-fs-amulya: Luxurious in a hushed way, Rosaline flows like pen-written lettering, its bright sharp edges set against fat dark stems. Amulya keeps its curves generously open and its strokes low in contrast, which is the whole appeal of the pairing: ornament above, plainness below.
gen-fs-rosaline-fs-plein: Rosaline enters on hairline strokes that lead into fat black stems, all flowing pen-written script, and it works well for a handful of lines. Plein gives each round letter a clear channel in, so a longer passage in this plain sans would read smoothly and without fuss.
gen-fs-rosaline-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans spaces its curve ends wide of the stems and draws its verticals and horizontals at identical weight, so no hairlines need squinting at. And Rosaline's fine hairlines against massive stems stay up top, since a long passage in this script would tire quickly.
gen-fs-rosaline-fs-synonym: Sharp, bright edges against fat darkness give Rosaline a hushed luxury, closed and pen-written. And Synonym, a plain sans of constant ink with open curves, is made for short stretches, so a slightly larger size would help it hold its own.
gen-fs-rosaline-plus-jakarta-sans: Bold downstrokes meet hairline upstrokes in Rosaline, a script that flows like fresh pen work and does its best in brief copy. Plus Jakarta Sans does the opposite, drawing round monoline letters like bent wire with curve endings kept well apart.
gen-fs-segment-fs-erode: Commanding and systematic, Segment spreads its letters out with a tall middle band that makes each line look stocky. Erode, a text serif with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, is comfortable in small doses and softens a longer read.
gen-fs-teko-gf-hepta-slab: Teko packs its steel-rod strokes tightly, with almost no gaps between letters, and it sounds confident from the first word. Yet Hepta Slab, a serif stretched wide with open counters and no thick-thin shifts, gives the pair its strongest quality: dense above, spacious below.
gen-fs-teko-gf-padyakke-expanded-one: Teko bends its strokes like steel rod and sets them tight, which is what it does best. But Padyakke Expanded One, a classic serif with wide-mouthed c shapes and round bowls of uniform walls, spreads its glyphs out like knots on a slack rope.
